idiom_name: Razor partial views (<partial name=... />) inside a layout with sections
implementation_notes: ASP.NET Core ships the whole pattern: a .cshtml file without an @page directive is a partial view, inserted with the Partial Tag Helper <partial name="_ProductRow" model="p" /> or with the async helpers Html.PartialAsync/RenderPartialAsync (RenderPartialAsync streams straight to the response), and _Layout.cshtml with @RenderBody()/@RenderSectionAsync()/-@section is the composite layout. Partials resolve by name through the view engine with no registration step; when a fragment needs real logic the official guidance is a ViewComponent (an invokable class returning IViewComponentResult) rather than a partial with embedded code.
code_sketch:
<!-- Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml -->
<header><partial name="_Header" /></header>
<main>@RenderBody()</main>
<!-- Views/Products/Index.cshtml -->
@model IReadOnlyList<Product>
@foreach (var p in Model) { <partial name="_ProductRow" model="p" /> }
pitfalls: Partials do not run _ViewStart.cshtml and are resolved through the view search path at render time, so a wrong or renamed name fails per request.

PartialAsync returns IHtmlContent while RenderPartialAsync streams; mixing the two - or calling the synchronous Partial/RenderPartial, which the docs warn can deadlock - corrupts or blocks the response.
A partial silently inherits the caller's ViewData/ViewBag; without an explicit model (via <partial model=...> or PartialAsync) the fragment's real inputs stay invisible and reuse breaks.
